summary: A Nielsen Norman Group explainer on empathy mapping, a UX research method that organizes user research into Says, Thinks, Does and Feels quadrants. It covers building a map, its uses, and common mistakes. A short section on AI says to use AI to organize existing evidence, not to generate evidence that doesn't exist. It does not discuss AI interfaces, agents, voice, or personal-context devices.
speakers_or_authors: Nielsen Norman Group (NN/g), UX research practitioners; no individual author named in the text.
relevance_reason: A general UX methods article. Its only AI content is a brief caution about using AI tools in empathy mapping, which is unrelated to how AI changes the way people interact with computers.
commercial_interest: NN/g sells UX training and consulting; the article is general guidance with no product promotion in the text.
older_event: Not an event-based item. It is evergreen method guidance, and nothing in it is news.
